plan.title: Lab 10 Windows route cannot pause for the required greeting edit

narratives.Description: The Lab 10 Native Windows route reaches READY and then treats a comment as though it returned control for the required greeting edit, so verification runs against the intentionally incomplete source. The accepted remedy splits the route at that manual boundary and adds an executable content lock for the fence ordering.
narratives.Overview:
## Situation

In `labs/10-implementation-golden-path.md`, the **Native Windows PowerShell 7.4+ route** is presented as one code block to run. It creates and installs the attempt, reaches `READY`, then contains only this comment:

```powershell
# Edit only (Join-Path $LabRoot "src/greeting.mjs") as specified in the implementation step.
```

The next statement immediately runs `implementation-lab.mjs verify`. A pasted PowerShell block does not pause at a comment, so the required manual edit cannot occur before verification.

## Pain

Following the documented Windows block literally caused verification to fail because `src/greeting.mjs` still had the intentionally incomplete implementation. I could complete the lab only by splitting the supplied route into undocumented segments, preserving `$LabRoot` myself, making the one-file edit, and then resuming verification.

This makes a correct learner run look like a product failure and requires the learner to redesign the control flow of the platform-specific route.

## Proposed fix

Split the Windows route into explicit phases:

- **Phase A:** create, guard, install, and run readiness through the `READY` checkpoint; print and retain `$LabRoot`.
- **Edit pause:** instruct the learner to edit only `src/greeting.mjs`, then run the documented one-file status/diff checkpoint.
- **Phase B:** verify, inspect evidence, reset, and archive using the retained root.

Alternatively, provide a deliberate interactive prompt/helper handoff that returns control after `READY` and explains exactly how to resume. A comment inside a monolithic pasted block is not a control-flow pause.

## Related but distinct

- #60 concerns the zsh-only starting-state check despite a later Windows route; it does not address the impossible manual-edit ordering inside this block.
- #64 reports the analogous generated-path pause in Lab 7 Task 5; this issue covers Lab 10's separate required product edit and verification failure.

No Directive source or framework internals were consulted.
narratives.UserStory: As a Windows learner completing Lab 10, I want the route to return control after readiness, so that I can make and inspect the one allowed greeting edit before verification.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Split the Native Windows route so Phase A ends after `readiness` and its READY guard, prints `$LabRoot`, and closes its PowerShell fence.
2. Add an out-of-fence instruction naming `Join-Path $LabRoot "src/greeting.mjs"` and the Task 2 one-file status/diff checkpoint before Phase B begins.
3. Keep Phase B limited to verification, evidence checks, reset, and archive, without adding an interactive prompt or helper wait verb.
4. Extend the Module 10 verifier and negative tests to parse the Native Windows fences and prove `readiness` occurs in an earlier fence than `verify`.

Round 1 fresh open critique of issue 65 at dispatch-sha `a484f30613f16d1da3c8f7a01edb5d67e562a12e`. Input ceiling 5785828929.

## 1. Split the Windows fences; keep the greeting edit out of the paste (sharpens-framing)

**Evidence.** `git show a484f30613f16d1da3c8f7a01edb5d67e562a12e:labs/10-implementation-golden-path.md` has one `powershell` fence at lines 282–306. Line 294 is `# Edit only (Join-Path $LabRoot "src/greeting.mjs") as specified in the implementation step.` Line 295 is `& node $Helper verify $LabRoot`. A pwsh probe that printed BEFORE, then that comment, then AFTER returned `BEFORE|AFTER` in one invocation. Piping `Read-Host` then `Write-Output "VERIFY-RAN"` into `pwsh -NoProfile -File -` made Read-Host consume the next line as the prompt answer (`Edit greeting then press Enter: Write-Output "VERIFY-RAN"`). `implementation-lab.mjs` `main()` dispatches only create, guard, install, readiness, verify, reset, archive. `node --test labs/fixtures/10-implementation-golden-path/test/greeting.test.mjs` failed 4/4 with actual `Hello!` versus `Hello, Ada!`. Existing pauses already in this tree: zsh Task 1 / Task 2 / Task 3 in the same lab; capstone Task 1 splits orient and activate across two fences with command-free prose between them (`scripts/verify-capstone.mjs` 638–651); Lab 2 Windows start prints `lab_root=` then sets `$env:LAB_ROOT` in a later command (`labs/02-disposable-initialization.md` 167–177).

**Failure mode.** A Bound-remedy that keeps one fence and inserts `Read-Host`, `pause`, or a new helper wait still reads the rest of a paste on stdin. A comment stays a no-op, so `verify` runs against `return "Hello!"`. Read-Host can swallow the verify line while reset and archive still run. A new helper verb also recuts the closed `main()` set.

**Disposition.** Bound-remedy is two or more PowerShell fences: Phase A through `readiness` and the READY throw; then an out-of-fence greeting edit plus the Task 2 `git -C $LabRoot` checkpoint; then Phase B `verify` through archive. Leave in-fence prompts and a new helper verb out of the harvest.

## 2. Name `$LabRoot` on the edit pause, because Phase A leaves cwd at `$Launcher` (sharpens-framing)

**Evidence.** Lines 286–288 create `$Launcher` under `[IO.Path]::GetTempPath()` and run `Set-Location -LiteralPath $Launcher` before `create`. `$LabRoot` is the helper OS-temp `repo`. The proposed edit line is "edit only `src/greeting.mjs`". zsh Task 2 already opens `$lab_root/src/greeting.mjs`. `verifyImplementation` requires `statusFiles` equal `["src/greeting.mjs"]` (`implementation-lab.mjs` 399–401).

**Failure mode.** After Phase A the working directory is the empty launcher. A relative `src/greeting.mjs` edit misses `$LabRoot`, so status stays empty and named CLI stays `Hello!`. Verification fails the same way the current paste fails.

**Disposition.** Phase A prints `$LabRoot`. The pause names `Join-Path $LabRoot "src/greeting.mjs"`. The one-file checkpoint uses `git -C $LabRoot`.

## 3. Lock the split on `scripts/verify-module-10.mjs` (sharpens-framing)

**Evidence.** `verifyModule10()` at this SHA returned `{ artifactCount: 27 }` while the one-fence defect exists. `markdownParts` strips fences, so `# Edit only` and `Helper verify` are absent from lab prose. `labHeadings` in `scripts/verify-module-10.mjs` 39–44 omits `Native Windows PowerShell 7.4+ route`. The capstone verifier already refuses one fence that contains both `orient` and `activate`. Lab 2's verifier already extracts `windowsStartBlock` from the PowerShell fence (`scripts/verify-modules-2-3.mjs` 518–525).

**Failure mode.** The markdown recut lands and a later edit merges the fences again; `npm run check:module-10` stays green.

**Disposition.** Extend `scripts/verify-module-10.mjs` and `scripts/verify-module-10.test.mjs` so the Native Windows section has at least two powershell fences, `readiness` in an earlier fence than `verify`, and a comment is not the separator. Reuse those existing fence-split checks.

## 4. P1 line range and candidate platform (footnote)

P1's 282–295 is the comment-then-verify locus; the fence continues through evidence, reset, and archive at 306. Phase B keeps that tail. The lab record and `verify-module-10.test.mjs` still treat Windows as a candidate; this recut leaves `windows-pwsh7` as candidate.

## Road not taken

Fence-split versus in-fence `Read-Host` versus a helper wait verb. Strongest rejected position: one paste with `Read-Host` keeps `$LabRoot` without a second session. That flips if a probe shows interactive pwsh running the whole fence as one script and blocking `Read-Host` on the console device without reading later script lines. Piped `pwsh -File -` filled the prompt from the next line. A helper wait would recut `main()` and the Module 10 verb list; the identity is the pasted block.
